summary: This Purgatorio lecture strengthens the Guide Trap map by showing that Virgil can illuminate Statius into poetry and Christianity while remaining unable to enter the truth his own light made visible.

existing_lens_links.concept: The Guide Who Becomes A Trap
existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Statius as the disciple who breaks Virgil's map of salvation from inside.
existing_lens_links.why_link_is_not_applied_now: The concept page needed a public extension first; episode-to-lens mark linking can follow after the new hover text is compiled and inspected.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Add the lamp-behind-him layer: a guide can produce light others use to transcend him, but his self-defense turns the disciple's ascent into a humiliation he cannot integrate.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Guide Trap owns this because the active mechanism is dependence on a necessary teacher whose world cannot survive correction. Free Will owns Statius trusting intuition and choosing ascent; Human Heart owns love as recognition or sharing; Stories/Poetry owns the medium by which Virgil's poem carries light.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Possible later pass: self-forgiveness and the will to cleanse in Purgatory intensify the self-made hell and non-coercive redemption material, but that would be a separate Free Will mutation.
